text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Chief arbiter for the disputed Bosnian town of Brcko Roberts Owen decides to award the town for one year to Bosnia's Serb republic, a source close to Moslem-Croat Federation representatives in the arbitration process says.
- Political parties in Bosnia's Moslem-Croat Federation deem the international arbitration panel's expected decision to award Brcko to Bosnian Serbs unjust.

- Moslem member of the Provisional Election Commission (PEC) of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) Kasim Begic says that the newly-established rules for local elections in Bosnia should correct most of, if not all, mistakes made at general elections held last September.
- Bosnia's Council of Ministers deputy co-premier Neven Tomic meets with U.S. State Department representative Thomas Briggs to discus Bosnia's arrangments with the International Monetary Fund (IMF).

- Moslem chairman of Bosnian collective Presidency Alija Izetbegovic has had a telephone conversation with U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright in which she informs him that significant changes took place in the arbitration panel's verdict on Brcko in favour of Moslem-Croat Federation.

- International High Representative for Bosnia, Carl Bildt, criticised for playing less than honourable role on the issue of Brcko, daily cites diplomatic sources as saying. During negotiations, Bildt said Brcko could not be handed over to the central government because he said the joint institutions essentially do not exist.
